title: unified-rollouts-add-preflight-probing-and-safety-guards
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Adds a preflight probing stage and safety guard improvements to the Unified Rollouts controller to reduce accidental regressions during canary/A-B/shadow deployments. Motivation: recent incidents showed a gap where a bad model could slowly degrade request quality before automated rollback triggered. This PR introduces a short preflight probing stage that runs a small, deterministic probing workload against new variants (canary/shadow) before routing live traffic, improves quarantine and manual-quarantine flows, and tightens metric quorum semantics for multi-metric autorollback. The change includes: 1) rollout controller changes to add 'preflight_probing' stage with configurable sample_size, timeout, and probe_workloads; 2) a probing engine that executes deterministic prompts and compares structured outputs against golden-response sets with configurable thresholds; 3) an enhanced quarantine policy allowing immediate manual quarantine, automated quarantine on quorum, and a delayed re-probing flow; 4) observability additions (new rollout_probing_duration histogram, probing_failure_reason tag, per-probe traces) and e2e tests simulating degradations; 5) API surface and CLI flags for customers to opt into preflight probing and set conservative defaults. Backwards compatibility: default remains off for existing rollouts; new rollout manifest fields are optional and validated. Rollout through canary/A-B/shadow flows is preserved and the autorollback engine now considers probing failures as first-class signals (with configurable weight). Security & perf: probing runs in a sandboxed worker pool and defaults to small sample sizes to avoid cost regression. Related: Linear ENG-2145 (proactive rollback improvements), ENG-2178 (probing harness).
